item.title: Stanford vandalism case ends in mistrial after ‘hopelessly deadlocked’ jury
item.description: A Santa Clara County judge declared a mistrial Friday in the felony vandalism case of five Stanford University students who had barricaded themselves in the president’s office during a spring 2024 protest in support of Palestine, after he found the jury to be “hopelessly deadlocked.” The post Stanford vandalism case ends in mistrial after ‘hopelessly deadlocked’ jury appeared first on Pleasanton Weekly.

item.title: Ex-GM Landreth alleges discrimination, corruption by East Bay Parks board in bombshell tort claim
item.description: Former East Bay Parks general manager Sabrina Landreth filed a tort claim against the district this week with a slew of allegations including gender-based discrimination, harassment and retaliatory conduct by board directors. The post Ex-GM Landreth alleges discrimination, corruption by East Bay Parks board in bombshell tort claim appeared first on Pleasanton Weekly.

item.title: Pleasanton council to review midyear budget, long-term financial forecast
item.description: The Pleasanton City Council is set Tuesday to discuss the city’s 2025-26 midyear budget update and the general fund’s long-term financial forecast, all of which set the scene on the city’s current financial health and what the next nine years might look like based on economic trends and potentially new revenue sources. item.description: A woman’s body was found in a restroom Saturday in the public lobby of the Santa Rita Jail in Dublin, the Alameda County Sheriff’s Office said. The post Woman found dead in restroom at Santa Rita Jail appeared first on Pleasanton Weekly.

item.title: ‘Go back to the drawing board’: BART directors, community react to potential station closures
item.description: BART’s Board of Directors met last week to get a clearer picture of what contingency plans are available to the cash-strapped agency – including abandoning both Tri-Valley stations in short order – if a ballot measure planned for this November fails to give it a financial lifeline.
